## NFL Transactions Briefing — 11/24

### Seahawks
- **Seahawks signed CB Trevon Diggs** in free agency.  
  **Impact:** Adds a notable name to the secondary and gives Seattle another option at corner.

- **Seahawks signed OL Bobby Hart** in free agency.  
  **Impact:** Veteran offensive line depth; likely a protection/insurance move up front.

- **Seahawks signed OL Chase Lundt** in free agency.  
  **Impact:** More line depth, suggesting continued attention to roster flexibility in the trenches.

- **Seahawks added RB Jacob De Jesus to the practice squad.**  
  **Impact:** Developmental backfield depth; no immediate fantasy relevance unless elevated.

- **Seahawks placed George Holani on Reserve/Injured.**  
  **Impact:** Removes a backfield depth piece from the active mix.

- **Seahawks waived DB Avery Smith.**  
  **Impact:** Clears a roster spot; depth in the secondary shifts elsewhere.

### Colts
- **Colts signed QB Shane Buechele** in free agency.  
  **Impact:** Adds quarterback depth and competition behind the top of the room.

- **Colts signed DL Carl Lawson** in free agency.  
  **Impact:** Boosts the defensive front with an experienced pass-rush/depth option.

- **Colts added ED Cameron Sample to the practice squad as a veteran.**  
  **Impact:** Experienced edge depth available if Indianapolis needs a call-up.

- **Colts placed Caden Curry on Reserve/Injured.**  
  **Impact:** Thins their defensive front depth.

- **Colts waived OL Charlie Heck.**  
  **Impact:** Opens a roster spot and reshuffles offensive line depth.

### Chiefs
- **Chiefs signed OL Fred Johnson** in free agency.  
  **Impact:** Adds offensive line depth and potential immediate insurance up front.

- **Chiefs placed Ben VanSumeren on Reserve/Injured.**  
  **Impact:** Costs Kansas City a depth piece; exact role impact is not specified.

### Giants
- **Giants signed RUSH Dawuane Smoot** in free agency.  
  **Impact:** Adds edge/front-seven help, likely aimed at rotational pass-rush depth.

- **Giants added OL Geno VanDeMark to the practice squad.**  
  **Impact:** Developmental offensive line depth.

- **Giants placed Greg Newsome II on Reserve/Injured.**  
  **Impact:** Secondary depth takes a hit.

### Eagles
- **Eagles signed LB Chance Campbell** in free agency.  
  **Impact:** Adds linebacker depth, likely for rotational or special teams help.

- **Eagles waived OL Jake Majors.**  
  **Impact:** Clears a roster spot and trims interior line depth.

### Steelers
- **Steelers added WR Brandon Smith to the practice squad.**  
  **Impact:** Extra receiver depth; mainly a developmental move unless elevated.

### Chargers
- **Chargers added RB Ian Wheeler to the practice squad.**  
  **Impact:** Backfield depth for the scout team and emergency elevation purposes.

- **Chargers waived WR Theo Wease Jr.**  
  **Impact:** Reduces wide receiver depth and opens a roster spot.

### Vikings
- **Vikings added OT Tristan Leigh to the practice squad.**  
  **Impact:** Tackle depth and a developmental addition for the offensive line.

### Raiders
- **Raiders added DL David Blay Jr. to the practice squad.**  
  **Impact:** Defensive line depth with no immediate active-roster guarantee.

### Falcons
- **Falcons waived LB Christian Harris (all contracts terminated).**  
  **Impact:** Atlanta moves on from a linebacker depth piece.

### Dolphins
- **Dolphins waived LB Shaka Heyward (all contracts terminated).**  
  **Impact:** Opens a roster spot and trims linebacker depth.

### 49ers
- **49ers waived WR Brandon Aiyuk (all contracts terminated).**  
  **Impact:** Significant receiver-room change on paper; further context is not specified here.

### Ravens
- **Ravens waived QB Kedon Slovis.**  
  **Impact:** Quarterback depth is reduced behind the active options.

### Jets
- **Jets waived DL Payton Page.**  
  **Impact:** Clears a roster spot and reduces defensive line depth.

### Titans
- **Titans waived LB Milo Eifler.**  
  **Impact:** Depth and special teams options at linebacker take a hit.

### Bears / Commanders
- **Bears claimed CB Isaac Yiadom off waivers from the Commanders.**  
  **Impact:** Chicago adds corner depth immediately; Washington loses a secondary piece.

## What matters most
- **Seattle was the busiest team** with multiple additions on the offensive line, a corner signing, a practice squad RB move, an IR placement, and a waiver.
- **Indianapolis made the most notable roster-volume push** by adding a QB, DL, and veteran edge depth while also making corresponding subtraction moves.
- **Chicago’s waiver claim of Isaac Yiadom** is one of the cleaner immediate-help moves, since waiver claims can lead to direct depth-chart consequences faster than most practice squad additions.
- **San Francisco waiving Brandon Aiyuk** is the most eye-catching transaction listed, though no further context is provided here.

## What to watch next
- Whether **Trevon Diggs, Carl Lawson, Fred Johnson, and Dawuane Smoot** are active quickly or remain depth pieces.
- If **Seattle’s offensive line additions** signal a broader issue with availability or performance up front.
- Whether **Shane Buechele** is simply emergency QB depth or part of a larger Colts quarterback-room adjustment.
- Whether **Isaac Yiadom** works directly into Chicago’s defensive back rotation.

### Injury briefing: key updates

**Chicago Bears**
- **Elijah Hicks** was a new addition to the estimated Tuesday injury report and has already been **ruled out**, per Ben Johnson.
- **Kyler Gordon** remained in the same status as Monday; no change was reported.
- The report was **estimated** because the Bears only held a walkthrough.
- **Why it matters:** Chicago’s secondary is thinner heading into the short-week game vs. Detroit.
- **Watch next:** Final Thursday status for the other listed Bears, especially Gordon.

**Baltimore Ravens / Houston Texans**
- **Derrick Henry** has been placed in the **concussion protocol** and would have been **limited** in Wednesday’s practice.
- Jesse Minter said Henry is **likely to play Sunday** vs. the Texans.
- **Why it matters:** Fantasy managers should still expect Henry to be active, but this is a status to monitor until the weekend.
- **Watch next:** Whether Henry gets upgraded from limited and clears the protocol cleanly.

**Week 12 early game note**
- **Kenneth Walker** was **ruled out** for Thursday night’s game.
- **Why it matters:** That’s a major backfield absence for Week 12.
- **Watch next:** Who absorbs the workload in his place.

**Green Bay Packers**
- **Micah Parsons** is returning from a **torn ACL** and is expected to make his debut Wednesday against the Rams.
- He’ll be on a **snap count**.
- **Why it matters:** Big boost for Green Bay’s pass rush, but not a full workload yet.
- **Watch next:** How many snaps the Packers actually give him.

**Los Angeles Rams**
- **Puka Nacua**’s MCL was reported as **“completely torn”**; he had knee surgery.
- Recovery is expected to take **at least four months**.
- **Why it matters:** The Rams are without their top receiver for a long stretch.
- **Watch next:** How Los Angeles replaces his production.

**Detroit Lions**
- Rookie DT **Skyler Gill-Howard** is out with a **season-ending injury**.
- **Why it matters:** Another hit to a banged-up Detroit defense.
- **Watch next:** How the Lions patch the defensive line depth.

- **Chimere Dike (WR)** — With Wan'Dale Robinson on IR, Dike has already taken over the vacated slot work: he logged 54 snaps last week, a season-high 60% slot rate, and led Tennessee in catches and receiving yards while adding six kick/punt returns for 127 yards. He looks like the clearest beneficiary of Robinson’s absence again this week, with both target volume and all-purpose usage intact. [4, 1]

- **Carnell Tate (WR)** — Tate returned from a two-game shoulder absence and immediately played 62 snaps while scoring on a 59-yard touchdown catch. He appears locked in as Tennessee’s WR1, so his route volume and red-zone upside stay near the top of the passing-game projection. [5, 4]

- **Calvin Ridley (WR)** — Ridley’s five-catch, 68-yard, TD line came on just 26 snaps and was driven mostly by garbage time. That keeps him in the lower end of the target tree behind Tate and Dike, making his weekly floor more fragile than the box score suggests. [3]

- **Tony Pollard (RB)** — Pollard remains the backfield engine, while Tyjae Spears is still only operating at about 70% and is effectively being managed. Michael Carter continues to handle Pollard’s breather/pass-protection work over Nick Singleton, so Pollard’s workload stays concentrated and Singleton remains a secondary change-of-pace option unless Tennessee expands him. [2]

- **Game script** — Jacksonville is a more than two-touchdown favorite, which points to Tennessee spending plenty of the afternoon in catch-up mode. That favors Cam Ward volume and keeps the Titans’ receivers more fantasy-relevant than the run game if the script turns pass-heavy early. [8]

That keeps Hill on the field enough to matter in fantasy, while Henry’s workload can still be nudged down if Baltimore leans into the same up-tempo split-back usage. [2]

Baltimore’s passing game is still distributing work between the top two rather than funneling through one alpha, so both project as co-anchors more than a single elite volume play. [2]

- **Mark Andrews (TE)** — Andrews played 40 snaps, but Matthew Hibner (35) and Josh Cuevas (15) kept the tight end rotation active behind him. That trims Andrews’ snap ceiling and leaves some route work split off instead of going to a full-time TE1 role. [2]

His offensive usage isn’t specified here, but a return role adds weekly utility and could keep him relevant on game day. [8, 10]
